blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank of India. It regulates the country's monetary system and manages the currency and credit system of the economy. It plays a vital role in maintaining financial stability and controlling inflation.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, following recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926).
Nationalized on January 1, 1949, under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
Serves as the sole authority for issuing currency notes in India (except one-rupee notes and coins, which are issued by the Ministry of Finance).
Controls credit and money supply through Quantitative tools (CRR, SLR, Repo, MSF) and Qualitative tools (Moral Suasion, Margin Requirements).
Governed by a Central Board of Directors consisting of the Governor, up to 4 Deputy Governors, and government-nominated directors.

blocks.content: • It was established under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
• The headquarters of RBI is located in Mumbai.
• To regulate the issue of banknotes.
• To maintain monetary stability in the country.
• To operate the currency and credit system.
The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country, responsible for regulating the issue of banknotes and securing monetary stability in India.

cells: RBI issues currency notes except one-rupee note.
RBI manages accounts of central and state governments.

blocks.content: • Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI lends money to commercial banks.
• Reverse Repo Rate – Rate at which RBI borrows money from banks.
• Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) – Percentage of deposits banks must keep with RBI.
• Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) – Percentage of deposits banks must maintain in liquid assets.

rows: Maintained in Cash, Gold, or Unencumbered Approved Securities
Maintained by commercial banks with themselves
No interest earned on CRR balance
Banks earn returns/yield on securities held under SLR
Regulates liquidity and controls credit expansion
Ensures bank liquidity and solvency to protect depositors

blocks.content: • Open Market Operations – Buying and selling government securities.
• Central Board of Directors – Governing body.

items: Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance) recommended the setting up of RBI.
Difference between Repo Rate (lending rate to banks) and Reverse Repo Rate (rate at which RBI absorbs liquidity).
CRR is kept with RBI strictly in cash form, whereas SLR is kept with banks themselves in cash, gold, or approved securities.
The Financial Year of RBI runs from April 1 to March 31 (aligned with the government fiscal year since 2020-21).

blocks.content: • RBI issues all currency notes except one-rupee note.
